title: Product total complexes compute cosimplicial homotopy limits
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring and let $K:\Delta\to\operatorname{Ch}(\operatorname{Mod}_\Lambda)$ be a cosimplicial diagram of unbounded cochain complexes [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. The category $\Delta$ has finite nonempty ordered sets $[n]=\{0,\ldots,n\}$ and order-preserving maps. Write $K^{n,q}=K([n])^q$, let $d$ denote its internal cochain differential, and let $\delta=\sum_{i=0}^{n+1}(-1)^i d^i:K^{n,q}\to K^{n+1,q}$ be the alternating sum of cofaces. Form the product total complex
$$\operatorname{Tot}_{\Pi}(K)^r=\prod_{n\ge0}K^{n,r-n},\qquad D=\delta+(-1)^n d\ \text{on bidegree }(n,q).$$
All products are taken in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. There is a natural equivalence $\operatorname{Tot}_{\Pi}(K)\simeq\operatorname{holim}_{[n]\in\Delta}K([n])$ in the enhanced derived category $\mathbf D(\Lambda)$, with homotopy limit interpreted by coherent limiting cones [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. This is an identification with the derived limit, and no boundedness in the internal degree is required. For a strict augmentation $a:\operatorname{const}(M)\to K$ of cosimplicial complexes, the map $M\to\operatorname{Tot}_{\Pi}(K)$ with degree-zero-cosimplicial component $a^0$ and all positive-cosimplicial-degree components zero represents the map from the augmented cone to that homotopy limit.

Here the enhanced derived category is presented by a homotopy coherent localization $q:N(\operatorname{Ch}(\operatorname{Mod}_\Lambda))\to\mathbf D(\Lambda)$ at the quasi-isomorphisms, in the sense of [def-coef-coherent-localization-interface]. The assertion holds in every such presentation; this specifies the enhancement, rather than taking the nerve of the ordinary derived category.

proof.text: Use the combinatorial projective model on unbounded $\Lambda$-module cochain complexes from [lem-coef-projective-cochain-monoidal-model]. The tensor/cotensor structures and Hom comparison of [lem-cbc-projective-cochain-dg-compatibility] give its dg-model structure over abelian-group complexes, and [lem-cbc-projective-cochain-suspension] gives stability. Apply [lem-coef-quillen-section-rectification] to the constant system of this stable combinatorial dg model category over the small category $\Delta$, with identity transition adjunctions and identity coherence maps. Its strict sections are precisely cosimplicial module complexes, equivalently complexes in $\mathcal P=\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta,\operatorname{Mod}_\Lambda)$. The cited theorem gives their projective model, with objectwise weak equivalences and fibrations, and identifies its enhanced localization, over evaluation, with $\operatorname{Fun}(N\Delta,\mathbf D(\Lambda))$. Every object of both projective models is fibrant, since maps to zero are degreewise surjective. These are exactly the model and coherent-diagram identifications used below.

proof.text: Construct a complex $P$ of covariant module diagrams by $P^{-n}([m])=\Lambda[\operatorname{Hom}_\Delta([n],[m])]$ for $n\ge0$ and $P^p=0$ for $p>0$. Here $\Lambda[S]$ is the direct sum of copies of $\Lambda$ on the basis $S$. Postcomposition defines the covariant diagram maps. The differential $P^{-n}\to P^{-n+1}$ for $n\ge1$ deletes one vertex with alternating signs: on $[x_0\le\cdots\le x_n]$ it is $\sum_{i=0}^n(-1)^i[x_0\le\cdots\widehat{x_i}\cdots\le x_n]$. Pairing the two orders of deleting two vertices gives square zero. The augmentation $\varepsilon:P\to\operatorname{const}(\Lambda[0])$ sends every degree-zero basis vertex to $1$. It is natural, since postcomposition preserves vertex deletion and the value $1$. Objectwise its augmented complex contracts: the map $h_n$ prepends $0$ to a vertex list, and $h_{-1}(1)=[0]$. Deleting the new first vertex yields the original list, and all other terms cancel against $h_{n-1}\partial$; thus $\partial h_n+h_{n-1}\partial=1$, including degree zero. This proves $\varepsilon$ is an objectwise quasi-isomorphism. The chosen contraction need not commute with all arrows of $\Delta$; only the augmentation and differential need be natural. For every possibly unbounded module complex $M$, the same objectwise contraction tensored with $M$ gives a chain homotopy equivalence $\varepsilon_M:P\otimes_\Lambda M\to\operatorname{const}(M)$, using the direct-sum tensor total. The cross terms cancel because the homotopy raises the chain degree of $P$ by one. This uses no flatness or bound on $M$.

proof.text: Each $P^{-n}$ is one free representable in the presheaf category on $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$. For a module diagram $V$, a map $\Lambda[\operatorname{Hom}_\Delta([n],-)]\to V$ is determined by the image $v$ of $1_{[n]}$, and has formula $[\alpha]\mapsto V(\alpha)v$. This proves the natural evaluation isomorphism without assuming a Yoneda theorem stronger than the displayed formula. Consequently the ordinary Hom complex $B(K)=\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_{\mathcal P}(P,K)$ has $B(K)^r=\prod_{n\ge0}K([n])^{r-n}$. The bounded-above/free-source assertion of [lem-cbc-presheaf-dg-function-complex], applied with its category $\mathcal C=\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$, says that this computes $R\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal P}(P,K)$ for arbitrary unbounded $K$, naturally in $K$. In particular $B$ sends objectwise quasi-isomorphisms to quasi-isomorphisms and sends objectwise acyclic complexes to acyclic complexes. All the products here are small by [def-weil-size-convention].

proof.text: There is an actual adjunction $L(M)=P\otimes_\Lambda M\dashv B(K)=\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_{\mathcal P}(P,K)$: the Hom differential is $d_Kh-(-1)^{|h|}h d_P$, and transposing a chain map in each tensor summand gives the adjunction on chain maps. Explicitly its unit sends homogeneous $m\in M^r$ to the graded map $p\mapsto(-1)^{r|p|}p\otimes m$. The products in Hom and sums in tensor express exactly the same family of bilinear maps, so no interchange of infinite sums and products is being assumed. The adjunction is Quillen for the models in Step 1. Indeed an objectwise degreewise surjection $f:K\to K'$ induces a degreewise surjection $B(f)$ by the product-of-evaluations formula of Step 3, choosing lifts coordinatewise. If $f$ is also an objectwise quasi-isomorphism, its kernel $E$ is objectwise acyclic: lift a cycle and correct its differential in the kernel, or use the elementary cycle/boundary argument for a surjective quasi-isomorphism. Step 3 makes $B(E)$ acyclic, and it is the kernel of the degreewise surjection $B(f)$. A surjective map of complexes with acyclic kernel induces an isomorphism on cohomology: lift a target cycle, correct its differential by a kernel boundary, and for injectivity subtract a lifted preimage of a target boundary before applying kernel acyclicity. Thus $B$ preserves fibrations and trivial fibrations. Adjunction of diagonal lifting problems then makes $L$ preserve cofibrations and trivial cofibrations.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-coef-model-infinity-derived-adjunction] to the Quillen adjunction of Step 4. By Step 2 the natural transformation $\varepsilon_M:L(M)\to\operatorname{const}(M)$ is an objectwise quasi-isomorphism for every $M$. In particular $L$ preserves all quasi-isomorphisms, since its natural augmentation compares it with the objectwise constant functor, which does. Step 3 says the same for $B$. The derived functors are therefore their directly localized functors, and section rectification from Step 1 identifies the localized $L$ with the constant-diagram functor. We obtain, naturally in every $M,K$, an equivalence of entire mapping spaces
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\mathbf D(\Lambda)}(M,B(K))\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(N\Delta,\mathbf D(\Lambda))}(\operatorname{const}(M),K).$$
The counit of this derived adjunction is a coherent cone $\operatorname{const}(B(K))\to K$, after inserting the inverse of $\varepsilon_{B(K)}$. The mapping-space equivalence is induced by composition with this very counit. The limiting-cone criterion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] therefore proves that this cone is limiting. Thus $B(K)$ represents the coherent homotopy limit, with its cone, and the derived-adjunction naturality makes the comparison natural in $K$. This argument proves a coherent limit, rather than only a universal property for degree-zero morphism groups.

proof.text: Under the evaluation isomorphisms of Step 3, write an element of $B(K)^r$ as $(h_n)_{n\ge0}$ with $h_n\in K^{n,r-n}$. The Hom differential has component $d_Kh_n-(-1)^r\delta h_{n-1}$, with $h_{-1}=0$, since precomposing a representable map with the deletion boundary evaluates to the alternating coface sum. Regrade the $n$th component in total degree $r$ by multiplication by $\epsilon(r,n)=(-1)^{rn+n(n-1)/2}$. The ratio $\epsilon(r+1,n)/\epsilon(r,n)=(-1)^n$ gives the internal-differential coefficient. The coefficient of the coface term is $-(-1)^r\epsilon(r+1,n)/\epsilon(r,n-1)=1$ for $n\ge1$. Hence this is a natural chain isomorphism $B(K)\cong\operatorname{Tot}_\Pi(K)$ with the stated differential $\delta+(-1)^n d$. In each output component only these two input components occur, so the formula makes sense on an infinite product for an arbitrary internal degree range. Composing its inverse with the limiting-cone identification of Step 5 gives the asserted natural equivalence.

proof.text: Let $a:\operatorname{const}(M)\to K$ be a strict augmentation. Under the derived adjunction of Step 5 its map to $B(K)$ is represented by the ordinary adjunction transpose of $a\varepsilon_M:P\otimes M\to K$. This follows from the stated unit/counit formula of [lem-coef-model-infinity-derived-adjunction]: both functors are homotopical, every target is fibrant, and on a cofibrant representative of $M$ it is the actual transpose; naturality then inverts the representative's quasi-isomorphism. Since $\varepsilon_M$ vanishes on every nonzero degree of $P$, the transpose has only its $n=0$ component, where $\varepsilon$ takes every vertex to $1$. Evaluation at $1_{[0]}$ makes that component exactly $a^0:M\to K([0])$. Equivalently, the unit formula from Step 4 followed by $a\varepsilon_M$ has sign $(-1)^{r|p|}=1$ on its only nonzero degree $|p|=0$. The regrading in Step 6 also has $\epsilon(r,0)=1$, so it preserves this map. Directly, it is a chain map because $a^0$ commutes with internal differentials and $\delta a^0=d^0a^0-d^1a^0=a^1-a^1=0$. Its image under the mapping-space equivalence is exactly the given augmented coherent cone, which proves the last clause as a statement about the specified map.

statement_change.old_statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring and let $K:\Delta\to\operatorname{Ch}(\operatorname{Mod}_\Lambda)$ be a cosimplicial diagram of unbounded cochain complexes [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. The category $\Delta$ has finite nonempty ordered sets $[n]=\{0,\ldots,n\}$ and order-preserving maps. Write $K^{n,q}=K([n])^q$, let $d$ denote its internal cochain differential, and let $\delta=\sum_{i=0}^{n+1}(-1)^i d^i:K^{n,q}\to K^{n+1,q}$ be the alternating sum of cofaces. Form the product total complex
$$\operatorname{Tot}_{\Pi}(K)^r=\prod_{n\ge0}K^{n,r-n},\qquad D=\delta+(-1)^n d\ \text{on bidegree }(n,q).$$
All products are taken in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. There is a natural equivalence $\operatorname{Tot}_{\Pi}(K)\simeq\operatorname{holim}_{[n]\in\Delta}K([n])$ in the enhanced derived category $\mathbf D(\Lambda)$, with homotopy limit interpreted by coherent limiting cones [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. This is an identification with the derived limit, and no boundedness in the internal degree is required. For a strict augmentation $a:\operatorname{const}(M)\to K$ of cosimplicial complexes, the map $M\to\operatorname{Tot}_{\Pi}(K)$ with degree-zero-cosimplicial component $a^0$ and all positive-cosimplicial-degree components zero represents the map from the augmented cone to that homotopy limit.
